chapter_title: The Second, concerning the Parable of the Tree.
chapter_note: The chapter opens in a Gospel-driven dialogue frame (Q&A + explicit Gospel citation) and then digresses into NT exempla (Judas/Paul) and sectarian polemic. The oldest teaching substrate emerges most clearly from ¶11 onward in systematic five-fold correspondences (five limbs/mental qualities mapped to cosmic hypostases and ships) and in the negative five-fold of the bad tree culminating in the "lump" and Darkness. Two strong institutional grafts occur as editorial seams (¶13, ¶16), where the correspondential pattern is extended to the holy church/catechumens/alms.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief editorial lead-in; not cosmological exposition, functions as chapter header/frame.
Dialogue frame + explicit Gospel citation formula (“As it is written in the Gospel…”) anchors this paragraph as NT-derived overlay.
Continues the beseeching/request frame and appeals to “scriptures”; functions as citation-driven setup rather than cosmological system teaching.
Sectarian polemic (“some among the sects…”) applies interpretation to contemporary groups rather than mapping within the cosmic system.
Hagiographic/compilational attribution (“our master Manichaios, the apostle of greatness”) plus polemical discussion; not a self-contained systematic cosmological mapping layer.
Continuation of argumentative exemplum about composite/natural mixture; lacks stable cosmos→cosmos correspondential mapping and reads as interpretive/polemical development.
NT narrative exemplum (Judas among the twelve; Satan entered him; handing the saviour to the Jews; crucifixion) entered via the Gospel tradition.
Continuation of the Judas exemplum; NT-derived narrative application.
NT narrative exemplum (Paul persecuting the church, revelation) is Christian overlay material, even where used to argue mixture.
Introduces interpretation explicitly through “the saviour preached in the parable”; the entry-vector is the Gospel parable rather than autonomous cosmological teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] how I will reveal to you [ ... ] the expound[er ... ] the trees [ ... ] the Father [ ... ] all of them, as he [ ... ] in the [ ... ] world [ ... ] this good tree, the [ ... ] the light of this good tree [ ... ] the Pillar [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Begins the internal cosmological identification of the good tree (Father/light/Pillar) without citing an external authority; the content pivots to cosmos-internal architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.20⟩ ... the intellectuals that are cloaked upon its body [ ... ] this good tree. They are the light elements that are mingled, being compounded in the totality.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmos-internal correspondential language (intellectuals/elements/mingling/totality) consistent with the systematic substrate.
Seam-extended correspondential pattern applied to institution (“holy church… teachers… catechumens”); by rule, entire paragraph is an editorial graft despite cosmic terms (Jesus the Splendour).

paragraphs.core_text: Behold, this is the good tree [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief transitional closure within the cosmological exposition; no citation or institutional application, though the deictic “Behold” is stylistically later-sounding.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] I reveal to you [ ... ] it has five limbs. [They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind.] [Its counsel] is the Pillar of Glory, the Perfect Man. [Its insight is the Fir]st Man who dwells in the ship of living waters. Its thought is the Third Ambassador [who dwells in] the ship of living fire, that shines in [ ... ] Also, the mind is the Father who dwells in greatness, who is perfect in the aeons of light.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the institutional graft within the five-fold mapping: “Its consideration is the holy church.” This clause shifts the correspondence from cosmos→cosmos to cosmos→contemporary institution, unlike the surrounding mappings to Pillar/First Man/Third Ambassador/Father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying core is a systematic five-fold (mental qualities ↔ cosmic hypostases/ships). The single identification with “holy church” is a later application crossing outside the cosmic system.
Seam-identified institutional material (alms, catechumens, purification in holy church); entire paragraph is pastoral graft onto the teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: It is consideration that shall [ ... ] they shall be raised up [ ... ] is counsel; they shall be raised up to insight, which is the First Man who dwells in the ship of the night; from insight they shall rise up to thought, which is the Ambassador who dwells in the ship of the day. And he too, great glorious thought, shall bring them in to mind; which is the Father, the God of truth, the great Mind of all the aeons of glory.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Classic substrate move: mental-process ascent mapped stepwise onto cosmic stations/ships and hypostases (First Man/ship of night; Ambassador/ship of day; Father/Mind). Impersonal/systematic sequence.
Reiterates the parable’s Gospel phrasing (“good tree… good fruit”) as a proof-text style closure; likely entered through the Gospel-parable overlay even without an explicit citation formula here.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.21⟩ [ ... ] bad [ ... ] happen in [ ... ] from [ ... ] also [ ... ] the way that it is [ ... ] the good tree [ ... ] of the fire [ ... ] they are the ruling-power [ ... ] heaven and the wheel [ ... ] they are the five fleshes that walk [ ... ] fruit [ ... te]aching as of error, the mystery that [ ... wh]ich Satan appointed in the world.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to cosmos-internal mechanics (ruling-power, heaven/wheel, five-fold structure, Satan as cosmic agent). Fragmentary but in the systematic explanatory register.
Application of the “taste” to contemporary opponents (“evil people, the sects… their teachers… law after law”); correspondence is used to point outward.
Appeal to “scriptures” plus master-attribution; functions as proof-text validation rather than autonomous cosmic mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.22⟩ [ ... I will] reveal to you and you [ ... ] The bad tree has five limbs. They are consideration, counsel, insight, thought, mind. Its consideration is the law of death. Its counsel is transmigration [ ... ] in type after type. Also, its insight is the furnaces of fire [ ... ge]henna; which is full of smoke. Thought [ ... ] vessel. Its mind is the [ ... ] the lump, the last bond, the [ ... ], they that Satan cast away [ ... ] the great [ ... ] and they fall [ ... ] the darkness [ ... ] all [ ... ] and they take away [ ... ] are swallowed in to the lump, and they are bound [ ... ] the fruit of darkness, the one that they [ ... ] for ever and ever [ ... ] his face [ ... ] will arrive at that place; and they have no repentance therein.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the outward-pointing application clause: “from which the sects take instruction.” The five-limb structure and eschatological/cosmic identifications otherwise remain within the system (law of death, transmigration, furnaces/gehenna, vessel, lump, Darkness, Satan).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core substrate is the negative five-fold mapping culminating in the “lump”/final bond and Darkness. A brief sectarian application intrudes into the otherwise cosmos→cosmos structure.

paragraphs.core_text: [ ... ] this is the explanation of the bad tree, as I have explained to you, which you [ ... ] to it [ ... ] good fruit [ ... ] its fruit bad [ ... ] in it, in its existent days [ ... ] in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Brief wrap-up of the systematic exposition; despite first-person pedagogy, it stays within the doctrinal explanation rather than institutional rule or citation.

paragraphs.core_text: it being changed from [ ... ] which lies in its good earth [ ... life] and light; as death and darkness do not exist [ ... ] Also, the bad tree is Matter [ ... ] it, I understand it alone among the [ ... wh]ich occurs in its bad earth [ ... ] darkness and death.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the direct-address/application lead-in: “Concerning this [ ... ] and my beloved ones [ ... ] them in truth,” which shifts voice to audience exhortation. Retained the creedal dualist identification (good earth/life-light vs Matter/darkness-death).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Underlying content is a compact dualist cosmological definition (good tree/good earth vs bad tree=Matter), but the paragraph opens with audience-address markers indicating later homiletic framing.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.23⟩ [ ... ] these two trees, and separates them one from another. He understands that they did not arise out of one another, nor did they come from one another. They did not come from one another. They did not come from one! The person who can separate them out may go up to the aeon of light,
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the beatitude-style exhortational frame at the start (“Blessed is every one…”) and removed the closing teacher-address clause (“[ ... as I have] revealed it to you.”). Retained the doctrinal assertions of non-derivation and absolute separation.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core doctrinal kernel: absolute dualism (no mutual arising; not from one). Later layer adds beatitude/exhortation and teacher-address closure.

paragraphs.core_text: And he sees [ ... ] bad fruit did not arise from it [ ... ]; but whoever will not separate out [ ... ] from one another, he falls to the land of darkness [ ... ] until he arrives at the [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Despite conditional language, the logic is cosmological-mechanical (separation vs descent to Darkness) and remains within the system (land of Darkness as eschatological destination).

Beatitude-style faith formula (“Blessed is whoever can believe!”) is characteristic of Christianized exhortation and likely entered through the Christian overlay stream rather than the impersonal cosmological substrate.
